transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2027-01-28 11:30 PST
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Ethan Park (Redwood CSM); Jordan Lee (CTO), Priya Menon (ML Eng), Marco Silva (Infra), Alicia Torres (Procurement)

Summary: quick walk through today's lab run, baseline numbers, tuning, and next steps. Customer concerned about p99 spikes under burst and overall unit cost compared to their incumbent provider. Redwood proposes dedicated slots + routing fallback if needed.

00:00 Jordan Lee: okay, everyone thanks for joining, we've got about 50 minutes, hope to finish with concrete next steps
00:18 Maya (Redwood): thanks Jordan. Quick agenda: run recap, latency delta vs incumbent, what we tuned, what stayed weird, then action items.
00:35 Priya (SilverCurrent): quick note, we ran the baseline again this morning on IncumbentCloudAI, same setup as last week, so numbers should be comparable.
00:48 Ravi (Redwood SE): great. So top-line: our median token latency was about 18ms lower, p95 about 30ms better, but p99 had a small group of spikes around 480ms when we hit concurrency bursts.
01:10 Marco (SilverCurrent): that p99 is the thing. our SLAs are very sensitive to 99.9 for some production paths, so even occasional spikes are risky.
01:22 Ethan (Redwood): understood — that's why we instrumented kv cache hit rates and router queue lengths. During the spike windows the KV cache hit rate dropped from 92% to 68% due to cold-cache churn on some prefixes.
01:38 Priya: does that mean cache warming or larger cache sizing?
01:45 Ravi: a mix. We saw a few patterns: long-tail sequences that touch expanded context, and also a concurrency bump that caused the runtime to evict earlier than ideal. Batching helped median but can increase tail unless we cap batch waiting time.
02:05 Jordan: can you remind us the incumbent numbers?
02:08 Priya: Sure — they showed median 12ms higher than Redwood, p95 25ms higher, and p99 was around 600ms under our synthetic workload. So Redwood is better on p99 in most windows but we saw those isolated spikes today that make it noisy.
02:28 Ravi: yes, exactly. The isolated spikes correspond to a mismatch in tokenization when we used a longer max-length in a few clients; that increased KV lookups and forced disk spill in the GPU memory path for one model variant.
02:48 Marco: oof disk spill, not ideal. Can that be eliminated?
02:52 Ravi: we have two levers: increase GPU KV memory (Dedicated slots), or switch to a quantized variant with more compact KV footprints. Both reduce spills. We tuned 4-bit quant and saw a 15% med latency hit but reduced p99 spikes substantially.
03:15 Priya: what's the quality delta on 4-bit quantization? Any hallucination or regression concerns?
03:22 Ravi: small degradation on few red-team prompts (we ran evals). Most of your prompt set stayed within tolerance; we can add a canary route so sensitive traffic uses full precision while bulk traffic uses 4-bit.
03:38 Jordan: routing policies — how easy is that to configure? And fallback if Dedicated isn't in place yet?
03:45 Maya: routing is policy-first in Redwood: you can set per-route model variants, percent splits, latency thresholds to trigger fallback to a cheaper/safer variant. We ship a default fallback that fails open to a smaller model or to incumbent if you prefer.
04:05 Marco: network wise — when you say fallback to incumbent, that's over which egress? will there be added latency for a double-hop?
04:12 Ravi: good question. In our config you choose where the fallback routes. For pilot we usually route to an internal compatible model hosted on Redwood Dedicated in a nearby region to keep latency comparable. If you route to a 3rd-party incumbent, yes you'd see additional transit latency.
04:35 Priya: can we see the exact config used in today's test? batch timeout, max batch size, cache sizes?
04:41 Ravi: yes — will share as part of the artifacts. Quick values now: batch_timeout_ms=8, max_batch_tokens=4096, kv_cache_entries=1.4M per GPU, quant profile=4bit-opt A.
05:02 Jordan: what's unit cost visible? you mentioned cost per 1M tokens earlier — how'd that compare to incumbent during the run?
05:10 Maya: rough numbers: Redwood run produced ~18% lower unit $/1k tokens at the observed throughput in this test, due to higher GPU efficiency and batching. However with Dedicated committed slots pricing, the per-token moves favor you more if steady throughput continues — could be 30% savings for long-running workloads.
05:35 Alicia (Procurement): we need the pricing sketch; show both on-demand and 3-month reserved.
05:40 Maya: we'll send both.
05:43 Priya: any security flags? we need SOC2 type 2, KMS integration and audit logs for token-level access.
05:52 Ethan (Redwood CSM): we have SOC2 docs, KMS/HSM integrations (customer-managed keys via Bring-Your-Own-Key), SAML SSO, fine-grained RBAC and token audit logs. We'll send the pack.
06:10 Marco: network egress — can we VPC-peering or do you need a NAT?
06:17 Ravi: for Private you can run the customer-managed control plane with direct VPC peering; on Dedicated we typically require customers to allow egress for telemetry; we'll share a minimal egress checklist.
06:30 Jordan: ok, I'd like to understand the head-to-head plan. What's the exact synthetic test you propose?
06:36 Maya: propose 30-minute run, 5k concurrent clients, ramp to 2k qps steady, with representative payload distribution Priya will provide. We'll capture med/p95/p99 and raw tail traces. We'll also run the incumbent with same workload and compare.
06:55 Priya: timeline ok — we can prep payloads by Friday. question: will Redwood run both in same region?
07:02 Ravi: yes, same region (us-west-2) for parity. We'll provide cloud VMs to run load driver or you can run from your infra — whichever you prefer.
07:18 Marco: about the p99 spikes — if Dedicated is used and we increase KV cap, that should remove disk spill, right?
07:25 Ravi: in our tests, bumping KV cache by 40% resolved the majority of the spikes for the longer sequences. Also warmup scripts before traffic bursts help.
07:35 Jordan: what about autoscaling behavior during the test? We saw some queuing last week when we hit a sudden ramp.
07:42 Ravi: the runtime uses continuous batching and autoscale policies; for pilot we can pin a minimal instance count and allow bounded autoscale to avoid cold-start churn. That produces stable tails at some incremental cost.
07:58 Priya: will you expose the routing and metrics dashboards during the test?
08:02 Ethan: yes — we'll provide read-only dashboard access to infra and ML leads. Dashboard will show token-level costs, queue lengths, per-model latency histograms and KV hit rates.
08:20 Alicia: procurement asks: what if we want to stop after 30 days? Any early termination fees for Dedicated pilot?
08:26 Maya: for pilots we usually sketch a short-term MSA with a 30-day exit clause; Dedicated reserved commitments are optional. We'll send the sketch.
08:40 Jordan: ok wrapping — I think the plan makes sense. Head-to-head then decision on short Dedicated pilot if p99 stable and unit cost target met.
08:50 Maya: reiterate next steps: Redwood to run head-to-head, share configs and pricing, customer to supply payloads and network details. Anything else?
09:02 Priya: just confirm we'll get the quant profiles and the perf artifacts.
09:08 Ravi: yes — I'll upload configs and the perf traces.

End notes: artifacts referenced: shared drive link (REDACTED) with logs, quant profiles, dashboard screenshots. Possible follow-ups: security deep-dive scheduled, Dedicated pricing sketch to be reviewed by Procurement.

Questions: (quick)
- Jordan: what happens if fallback triggers 20% of requests? will that hide real issues?
- Ravi: you can throttle fallback rate and monitor per-route quality to avoid masking; we'll set alerting on fallback rate.

Crosstalk/fillers present throughout. Transcription contains minor name miscaptures (e.g., 'kv cache' sometimes transcribed as 'K-V cache'), occasional punctuation errors.
